column3: Judgments of first-instance and personal-status courts; not in urgent matters.
An agreed suspension lasts at most three months. The case must be resumed within 15 days after the suspension ends, or the petition is void. Counted from the end of the suspension.
If the plaintiff does not continue the case within six months, the petition is void. Proposed from the session; move the start to the day the other question is decided if that is later.
A case interrupted (death or loss of capacity of a party) and not continued within six months without an acceptable excuse is void. The interruption also halts the periods running in the case.
When the judgment rests on fraud or forgery, the period counts from the day it is discovered.
Art. 204 also names judgments of first-instance courts. The period is proposed for judgments of the courts of appeal; add it by hand where cassation of a first-instance judgment applies.
The article's text is verified; applying it to personal-status judgments follows the Supreme Judicial Council's commentary.
Urgent and ancillary decisions such as a precautionary attachment. Add it to the matter from the decision's notification.

Counted from the day after the fraud or forgery is discovered or proven.

When both parties are absent the court leaves the case for review; unless a party asks to renew it within the period, the petition is void. Older sources give 30 or 15 days: check the current text.
Defamation, threats, some thefts and breaches of trust: the complaint must be made within three months of the day the victim learns of the offence.
Unless the person convicted in absence surrenders or objects within the period, the judgment counts as given in presence.
Unless the person convicted in absence surrenders or objects within the period, the judgment counts as given in presence. Added by hand: the court alone does not tell a violation from a misdemeanour.
Counted from the day after the pronouncement when the judgment is given in presence, not from its notification; a judgment given in absence counts from the notification.
Counted from the notification to the convicted person, or from the arrival of the papers at the trial court.

A debtor who pays within the period is exempt from the collection fee. Older texts give other periods, and a government debtor may have 30 days (Art. 20): verify. Proposed when an execution stage records the date the notice was served.
